newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China yearly growth seen at 8.7 percent - UN unit.
newsitem.headline: China yearly growth seen at 8.7 percent - UN unit.

text.p: China's annual economic growth should average 8.7 percent from 1996 through the year 2000, a United Nations unit said on Wednesday.
The 1997 survey by the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific forecast gross domestic product (GDP) growth rates for South Korea at 6.6 percent and Taiwan at 6.2 percent.
Behind the East Asian pack was Hong Kong, with growth projected at an average 4.4 percent.
The survey put Chinese inflation at an average 8.2 percent, through 1999 rather than 2000 and using gross national product deflators.
South Korea's inflation was projected at an average 3.8 percent through 2000. Taiwan's was forecast at 0.4 percent using GDP deflators.
Hong Kong inflation was projected at an average 6.9 percent through 1999 using GDP deflators.

The report, released through Singapore's Trade Development Board, said Hong Kong, South Korea and Taiwan are among areas where growth is "expected to record a more pronounced slowdown as a natural consequence of maturing economies".
